summary: Sokatsu Shaku worked in Buddhist studies, studying under traditional teachers Kōsen Imakita (1889) and Soyen Shaku (1893–1898). He founded Ryobokai in 1901, the Ryobokai Dojo of North America in 1906, and Ningen Zen.

Active in Buddhist studies, Sokei-an Shigetsu Sasaki studied at Tokyo Academy of Fine Arts/Tokyo University of the Arts (~1900–1905), San Francisco Art Institute, and California Institute of the Arts. He studied under Sokatsu Shaku and Soyen Shaku, and founded the First Zen Institute of America in 1930.

Specializing in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology, Sokichi Tsuda studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō (~1890–1891). He worked at the SMR Research Department (~1908–1919), Waseda University (~1920–1940; founded 1935), and the University of Tokyo (~1938–1940).

Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Soko Morinaga studied at Toyama High School (~1943–1947), Daitoku-ji (~1948–1963), and under Zuigan Goto and Sesso Oda. He served as head of Hanazono University (1986–1994) and abbot at Daishuin (~1963–1995).

Sokuo Eto, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Komazawa University (1904), Kyoto University (graduated ~1909–1912; doctorate by 1944), and the University of Tokyo. He founded Dokenryo in 1937 and held posts at Komazawa Junior College (~1950–1958) and Komazawa University (1953).

Solomon Caesar Malan specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at St Edmund Hall, Oxford (1833) and the University of Edinburgh (D.D. by 1880), and held posts at Bishop's College, Calcutta (1838), The Asiatic Society (~1838–1840), and Balliol College, Oxford (1843).

Specializing in Tibetology, history, and archaeology, Solomon George FitzHerbert earned a doctorate from the University of Oxford. He served as a Departmental Lecturer at Oxford and held a researcher post at the National Centre for Scientific Research (attested 2019).

Active in Buddhist studies, Soma Thera was educated at St. Benedict's College, Colombo, and studied under the traditional teacher Jetavana Sayadaw in 1936. Around 1929, he was a member of Servants of the Buddha.

Somadeva Vasudeva is an Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford, Columbia University, Clay Sanskrit Library, Kyoto University, the French Institute of Pondicherry, and Oxford.

Somboon Watana specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Panjab University in 1999 under Rekha Jhanji and Dharmanand Sharma, and was an Assistant Professor at Mahidol University (attested 2026).

Active in Buddhist studies and philosophy, Somchai Kusalacitto earned a Ph.D. from the University of Madras. He served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2003).

A Buddhist studies scholar, Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara studied at Wat Bowonniwet Vihara (~1933–1941) and under Swami Satyananda Puri and Vajirayanavangsa. He was abbot of Wat Bowonniwet Vihara (~1961–2013), Director at Mahamakut Buddhist University (1961), and taught meditation at Kasetsart University (1976).

Somphong Santacitto is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master's Degree in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Suthithammanuwat (attested 2006).

Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, Somsak Phansiri earned a Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Madras (2005–2011) and served as a Lecturer at Buriram Rajabhat University in 2026.

Sonam Chhoki specializes in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She earned an M.A. from Jawaharlal Nehru University and a Ph.D. from SOAS University of London, and worked as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.

Sonam Choden works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. As of 2026, she is attested as a doctoral local researcher and project collaborator (Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin) at the University of Hamburg.

Sonam Gyatso is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He worked as a research assistant at Toyo Bunko (~1961–1967) and later served as a Professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014).

Sonam Jamtsho is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who has been a doctoral local researcher and project collaborator (Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter) at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Sonam Kachru works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Chicago (2006–2015) under Dan Arnold. He held fellowships at Forum Transregionale Studien and the Max Planck Institute, and became Assistant Professor at Yale University in 2022.

Sonam Kinga specializes in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at Sherubtse College (~1994–1998) and Kyoto University (Ph.D., 2007–2010), was a researcher at the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH (~1999–2007), and joined Aarhus Institute of Advanced Studies in 2026.
